issue.title: Add All-Takes View with Canonical Selection to Record Tab
issue.body: The Record Tab (#71) shows only the active account's takes. In team recording sessions, translators take turns with a shared device: each switches to their own account, records takes for a passage, then the group listens back together and agrees on the one take to carry forward into checking. This ticket adds the cross-account layer: a toggle that surfaces takes from all device accounts for the current unit, attributed by recorder, with a canonical designation control that marks the take advancing through the checking workflow. ## Functional Requirements ### Take View Toggle - Display a segmented control above the take list with two options: "My Takes" and "All Takes." - Show the toggle only when at least one other account on the device has recorded a take for the current unit; hide it otherwise. - Default to "My Takes" each time the Record Tab is opened. - "My Takes" view is unchanged from #71: shows only the active account's takes with all existing controls. ### All Takes View — Take List - Display takes from all accounts on the device for the current unit, grouped by account. - Each group is preceded by a header row showing the account holder's display name and a `li:user` icon. - Within each group, takes are ordered by take number ascending. - Each take card shows: take number, compact inline waveform, duration, and a `li:play` / `li:pause` button. - Tapping `li:play` on a card plays that take inline; playback of one take stops any other take currently playing. - Each take card shows a canonical indicator on the trailing edge: `li:circle` when undesignated, `li:circle-check` when this take is the canonical selection. ### All Takes View — Canonical Selection - Any account logged in on the device may designate a take as canonical from the All Takes view. - Tapping `li:circle` on a take card designates that take as canonical; the icon changes to `li:circle-check`. - Only one take across all accounts may be canonical at a time; designating a new take removes the indicator from the previously designated one. - The canonical designation may be changed at any time by any account on the device. - Canonical designation does not trigger a sync; it is included when the take's owning account syncs under normal rules. ### All Takes View — Restrictions - "Record New Take" does not appear in All Takes view. - Delete controls do not appear on take cards in All Takes view. - Active-draft selection (the highlighted border and `li:circle-check` from My Takes) does not appear in All Takes view; the only action available on a take card is play/pause and canonical designation. ### My Takes — Selection Behavior - When the toggle is hidden (only one account has takes for the unit), My Takes shows the active-draft selection indicator exactly as defined in #71: one take is selected, shown with `li:circle-check` and a highlighted border. - When the toggle is visible (multiple accounts have takes), the active-draft selection indicator is hidden in My Takes; canonical designation in All Takes is the only selection available. - If the active account's own take is the current canonical selection, that take card displays a read-only `li:circle-check` on the trailing edge. - If the canonical take belongs to another account, no canonical indicator appears on any take card in My Takes view. ### 5-Take Cap - The 5-take cap is enforced per account, not per device. - Each account may record up to 5 takes for a unit regardless of how many takes other accounts have recorded for the same unit. > **Note:** The canonical designation introduced here is the same mechanism the conflict resolution workflow uses to mark the take that advances through checking (see #256 and related MCR tickets). Engineers should wire both to the same underlying flag rather than creating a parallel concept. > **Note 2:** The per-account 5-take cap defined here supersedes the ambiguous cap language in #71, which does not address multi-account scenarios.
